symptoms: Blisters/vesicles on hooves, mouth and tongue
immediate_actions: ISOLATE the animal from the herd immediately
Do NOT move the animal off the farm
Report to local veterinary/animal husbandry authority (legally required)
Restrict visitor access to the farm

treatment.description: No specific cure exists. Supportive therapy: clean and disinfect lesions, provide soft feed and clean water. Antibiotics for secondary infections only.
treatment.first_aid: Wash lesions with 0.2% citric acid or potassium permanganate. Apply glycerine + iodine to mouth lesions. Provide soft feed and clean water.

FMD.prevention: Vaccinate entire herd with polyvalent FMD vaccine every 6 months. Disinfect shed with 2% sodium hydroxide. Strict biosecurity — no sharing of equipment. Restrict visitor access.

symptoms: No visible signs of disease detected

treatment.description: Continue regular feeding, vaccination schedule, and routine health checks.
treatment.first_aid: No immediate treatment required. Continue routine preventive care.

Healthy_Cow.prevention: Maintain vaccination schedule. Regular deworming every 3 months. Clean water supply and balanced TMR diet. Regular health checkups every 6 months.

symptoms: Multiple raised firm nodular skin lumps (2-5 cm diameter)
Skin lesions may ulcerate and become necrotic
immediate_actions: Vaccinate the remaining herd within 48 hours
Control insects (flies, mosquitoes, ticks) — they spread the virus

treatment.description: Supportive care. Treat secondary skin infections. Anti-inflammatory for fever. Keep animal in clean, dry, shaded area.
treatment.first_aid: Clean nodules with warm saline water. Apply neem + turmeric paste or Betadine. Maintain dry shaded bedding.

LSD.prevention: Annual LSD vaccination with live attenuated vaccine. Insect vector control with permethrin sprays. Quarantine new animals for 28 days. Disinfect shed daily during outbreaks.

symptoms: Hot, swollen, red or hard udder
immediate_actions: Milk the affected quarter more frequently (3-4x per day)
Do NOT consume or sell the affected milk
Collect milk sample for bacterial culture if possible

treatment.description: Intramammary antibiotic infusion. Anti-inflammatory treatment. Strip affected quarter frequently.

medicines.name: Amoxicillin/Cloxacillin intramammary tube
medicines.dosage: One tube per quarter, twice daily for 3 days

treatment.first_aid: Wash udder with warm water. Fore-strip and discard infected milk. Post-dip teats with 0.5% iodine after milking.

Mastitis.prevention: Post-milking teat dipping with iodine-based solution. Dry cow intramammary therapy. Regular milking hygiene. Keep milking equipment clean and calibrated.
